scope: First architecture review of the accounting cases H-1, H-4 and H-5 and the resulting fixes, with local mock checks. No PostgreSQL ran.

keyConclusions: No path to a false PASS, an under-count or double-count of an active charge, a hidden foreign or second marked job, or the CRASHED record treated as settled.
The ONE-form subtraction runs only after CRASHED, PAUSED and lease or status mismatches are refused, and the residual must equal the W7 view exactly.
Donor rows come from the product runtime; copies use INSERTs with every key and trigger active; no replication-role change and no write to any W7 row.

fixes: m0 builds use baseJobs null as production does; a non-null value needs an explicit label (one labeled strict variant remains).
The H-4 donor is disposed before the job fixtures; the computed connection peak drops from 9 to 5 of 9 usable.
H-5 stores the measured H-4 values and passes only when H-4 passed.
The lapse check reads 32 pinned product modules in H-1 and H-4; consumer worlds record lapseChecked 0 with the reason.
H-4 compares an independently computed job hash and the residual counts with the donor counts.
A W7 record revision drift must give ALLOWLIST_RECORD_CHANGED without touching donor rows.
Runtime failure and cleanup-timeout codes are no longer masked as fixture cleanup failures.
The first real run records the operations at the completing pause, the queued update result and the JSON round trip.
firstRealRunObservations: code for each H-1 and H-4 label
operations at the PROFILE_COMPLETING pause (expected ACTIVE; STOP_REQUIRED would be a harness fix)
JSON round trip of copied rows
peak connections from pg_stat_activity, wall time and peak memory
residualFindings: H-5 evidence lacks the synthetic-authority labels that H-1 and H-4 carry (not a regression).
Coverage gaps carried over from the legacy harness: no foreign ledger with an open operation during the ONE form, no PAUSED marked job, no active job created before the anchor.
limitations: No PostgreSQL ran: every code, operation and count in these cases is a reasoned expectation until the first real run.
Native dependency graph unsealed; no Linux adapter; current VPS health and identity unknown.
nextAction: Build the sealed Linux package and execution adapter, then prepare a read-only capability and health packet that also records one raw Job line, and the isolated PostgreSQL harness packet, each with a fresh owner GO.
